synopsis: Chile relies on national workplace and mining regulation rather than a continent-wide South American machinery regime; its Decreto Supremo 132 provides broad mining safety and equipment controls [f2285, f2291]. DS 132 was promulgated in 2002, published on 7 February 2004, and reviewed in a consolidated version incorporating amendments through 2024 [f2290]. The booklet found no dedicated automatic-braking performance or test standard in the reviewed DS 132 material, while SERNAGEOMIN guidance and Codelco standards were not verified [f2292, f2293]. These findings mean numeric acceptance items were “not found,” not that they are “not required”; the booklet also found no dedicated Chilean off-road rule requiring an ML-based collision-avoidance function to meet a specified ML validation standard by 2028 [f15586, f2393].
